title: 2017 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: The ratio of the short side of a certain rectangle to the long side is equal to the ratio of the long side to the diagonal. What is the square of the ratio of the short side to the long side of this rectangle?

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) and \(y\) be the short and long sides, so the diagonal is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) and \(\dfrac{x^2}{y^2} = \dfrac{y^2}{x^2 + y^2}.\) Writing \(r = \dfrac{x^2}{y^2},\) the right side is \(\dfrac{y^2}{x^2 + y^2} = \dfrac{1}{r + 1},\) so \(r = \dfrac{1}{r+1},\) giving \(r^2 + r - 1 = 0.\) The positive root is \(r = \dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: With short side \(x\) and long side \(y,\) the diagonal is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2};\) write \(\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}\)
Let \(r = \dfrac{x^2}{y^2}.\) Squaring the ratio equation gives \(\dfrac{1}{r} = r + 1\)
